D.treatment: adults served by the public and private educational system

O.outcome_detail: share and estimated number of low-skilled adults receiving education or training

cells.quote: To review, 36 million American low-skilled adults can benefit from some form of education and training, including adult basic education, English as a Second Language (ESL), high school equivalency exam preparation, computer literacy, and other job-based skills. But only 11 percent of those adults are currently being served by the public and private educational system. Technology-based solutions have the potential to scale learning programs to the remaining 89 percent of adults, if we start to invest more actively in the adult learning market.
cells.note: This is a market-size estimate rather than an effect comparison; the study does not report a learning outcome or effect size.
